description: Five orientation callouts for the unannotated virtual-20261124-take4 edit. Coordinates are source pixels; times are playback seconds.

text: One ground robot. Two position estimates.

runs.text: Blue: GPS + wheels + IMU + UAV corrections.

text: Blue controls the robot; orange is comparison.

target.description: Early recorded tracks of the same UGV near the start. Actual, cooperative and baseline tracks remain visible below the panel.

callouts.purpose: Identify one physical robot, simulator truth, both estimators and which estimate controls navigation before the first detour.

text: The drone's downward camera builds this map.
Gray: detected obstacles. Purple: robot clearance.
White, blue and orange trace past positions.

target.description: Persistent gray occupied camera-map cells at the upper cylinder. The cyan intended route and recorded position tracks remain visible below.

callouts.purpose: Explain camera-map provenance, obstacle clearance and the difference between planned motion and recorded position histories.

runs.text: Yellow dots: GPS readings from the ground robot.

text: Their spread shows simulated measurement noise.

target.description: The persistent yellow color key identifies the GPS scatter. No pointer follows an individual fix because plotted dots fade after six browser wall seconds.

callouts.purpose: Identify noisy UGV GPS position reports well before the noise and outage controls.

text: Paired speeds are the model's input.

runs.text: Cyan: speed requested by the drive controller.

text: A window pairs the latest 100 wheel samples
with commands at matching sample times.

target.description: Orange measured wheel speed and cyan command reference in the upper ML plot. The panel sits on empty Gazebo ground below the physical robot; dashboard plots and telemetry remain visible.

callouts.purpose: Define the controller command as the wheel-speed reference and explain the 100 acquisition-matched paired samples at ML chapter entry.

text: Each model check scores a window

target.description: The live wheel-score and consecutive-window counter at the top of the dashboard. This panel begins before the first recorded 3/3 published fault.

callouts.purpose: Explain that three counts distinct consecutive model decisions over overlapping wheel-speed windows, rather than sensors, fault types, training failures or trials.
